title: How far does the tortoise walk in three hours?
description: The tortoise walks one quarter of a kilometre each hour, and the video finds the distance for three hours by adding the same walk three times. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that the three should also multiply the bottom number.
teaching_notes: One idea: a whole number times a fraction is the same fraction added again and again, so only the count of parts grows. Watch for students who multiply the whole number into both the top and the bottom of the fraction.

source: Laksh's pet tortoise can walk 1/4 km in 1 hour. How far can it walk in 3 hours?
video_script.why: The child has met whole number distances and now sees the same multiplication work when the distance of one hour is a fraction.
video_script.substitution: Three hours means one quarter added three times, which is three quarters.
video_script.anchor: Laksh's pet tortoise walks one quarter of a kilometre in one hour: how far in three hours?
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the three into both the top and the bottom of one quarter and gets three twelfths, which is only one quarter again
video_script.payoff_line: The tortoise can walk three quarters of a kilometre in three hours
video_script.fraction_reading: one quarter, three quarters, three twelfths

names.Laksh: walks 3 km in 1 hour; his pet tortoise walks 1/4 km in 1 hour

maths_rules: the slip: 3/12 = 1/4, the distance of one hour
video_script.design: One idea: multiplying by a whole number adds the same fraction again and again. The number line with three stretches of one quarter is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a line from zero with the tortoise at the start and a mark at 1/4 km for 1 hour; a question mark at 3 hours

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.walk: the mark at one quarter of a kilometre is placed for one hour
marks.ask: a question mark appears at three hours

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about Laksh and a pet tortoise.
<bookmark mark='walk'/>The tortoise can walk one quarter of a kilometre in one hour.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How far can the tortoise walk in three hours?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the line from zero is cut into three equal stretches, each one hour long; each stretch is one quarter of a kilometre

marks.line: the line from zero is drawn
marks.stretch: one stretch for one hour lights up
marks.three: three stretches are laid one after the other

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Draw a line that starts at zero.
<bookmark mark='stretch'/>One hour of walking is a stretch of one quarter of a kilometre.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three hours of walking means three such stretches, one after the other.

marks.given: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the tortoise walks one quarter of a kilometre in one hour.

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the distance the tortoise walks in three hours.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, find the distance by multiplication, as for whole numbers.
Three hours is three times one hour. We multiply three by one quarter of a kilometre.

marks.add: the three equal quarters are written with plus signs

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, three times a number means adding that number three times.
We add one quarter, one quarter and one quarter.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Three parts, each one quarter, make three quarters.
The tortoise can walk three quarters of a kilometre in three hours.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 3 × 1/4 = 3/12 is written and crossed out; a note shows 3/12 is the same as 1/4, the walk of one hour; three stretches of one quarter are shown again

marks.fix: the note 3/12 = 1/4 appears and the line is crossed out
marks.rule: the three stretches glow, and the bottom number is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is three twelfths of a kilometre.
Keeko multiplied the three into the top and the bottom.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But three twelfths is the same as one quarter of a kilometre, the walk of one hour.
The tortoise must walk further in three hours.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The three tells us how many quarters we add. Each quarter keeps its size, so the bottom number does not change.
